newsitem.title: UK: IBCA confirms Swiss Bank Corp ratings.
newsitem.headline: IBCA confirms Swiss Bank Corp ratings.

text.p: European rating agency IBCA said on Wednesday it confirmed Swiss Bank Corp's long-term AAA, short-term A1 plus, individual A/B and legal 1 ratings.

"This follows today's announcement that, with effect from the publication of its figures for 1996, SBC intends to adopt a seemingly innovative method of reporting its credit loss experience, which will take account of the inherent loss potential built into its portfolio of credit risk, both on and off balance sheet," IBCA said in a statement.
Its calculations show a need for an initial reserve of two billion Swiss francs which SBC will initially top up with an additional 400 million "safety margin", IBCA said.
IBCA said the initial reserve will result in a reported loss of around 1.9 billion francs for 1996.
"Nevertheless, in IBCA's judgment, nothing will have changed in terms of maintainable profit," the agency said. "Indeed 1996 should prove to have been a considerably better year for SBC than 1995."
While there will be a diversion of retained earnings from published equity to the new reserve, IBCA said it will not make any difference in practice to the amount of reserves available to cover risk.
"It will, however, have the useful cosmetic effect in future years of making the group's reported return on equity higher than it would have been under the existing reporting format."
IBCA said the change had no implications of substance for its SBC ratings.
